answer: Picture the agent economy as a meadow where every participant must carry a yarrow sprig: a hardware-bound identity card. Each agent generates its keypair inside a TPM chip, which attests one machine equals one identity. The network verifies it, issues a credential, and rejects any second registration from the same chip. Forging 10,000 fake identities needs 10,000 TPM chips at $20 each ($200,000) plus 30 days to provision them one by one. A sybil swarm is like repainting a meadow with one pigment: the color matches, but every blade still needs its own root.
